prior_suggestions.start_name: Edfu city, Aswan Governorate, Egypt (delivery point — sugar/paper factories + city households)
prior_suggestions.end_name: National-grid tie-in point on the South Valley / 'Upper Egypt' Gas Pipeline trunk (Dahshour–Aswan), likely near Kom Ombo or the Aswan terminus — exact tie-in point not sourced
prior_suggestions.corridor_desc: The GASCO 930km Dahshour–Aswan trunk (GEM P0477 / 'Upper Egypt Gas Pipeline') terminates at Aswan city (independently confirmed via a 2010 inauguration report and the EIB project page). The 37km Edfu line is a short terminal extension/spur south of that trunk, running along the Nile Valley corridor (west or east bank, unconfirmed which) toward Edfu town, ~45–55km north of Aswan and passing near or through the Kom Ombo area, where Arabic-language reporting independently documents a gas pressure-reduction/metering station used to distribute gas onward to Edfu, Kom Ombo and Nasr al-Nuba villages. The precise tie-in point (Aswan city vs. a point nearer Kom Ombo) is not established in sourced material — do not treat the waypoint/end coordinates as the confirmed route, only as the best-defensible corridor bound.
